subject: ela
title: Main Idea Detective
objective: Identify the main idea of a nonfiction passage and support it with two details.

visual.title: Evidence detective board
visual.caption: A visual board with a main idea clue in the center and detail cards connected around it.

teachingSupport.summary: A main idea is the big point that the strongest details all help prove.
teachingSupport.description: Learners use a detective board to sort details, reject distracting facts, and defend one main idea with proof.

diagramCallouts.title: Main idea
diagramCallouts.body: Put the big point in the center only after checking several details.

diagramCallouts.title: Proof details
diagramCallouts.body: Details should connect back to the center idea, not just sound interesting.

diagramCallouts.title: Distractor detail
diagramCallouts.body: A fun fact can be true and still not prove the main idea.

helperNotes: Ask: What do most of these details have in common?
Use two proof cards before writing the final sentence.
Have the learner explain why one detail does not belong.

commonMisunderstandings.mistake: Choosing the first sentence as the main idea every time.
commonMisunderstandings.fix: Check whether every detail supports it before accepting it.

commonMisunderstandings.mistake: Picking an interesting detail instead of the big point.
commonMisunderstandings.fix: Ask whether the detail is one clue or the whole message.

teachingSupport.confusionPrompt: Write whether you are stuck finding the big idea, choosing proof details, or rejecting distractors.

funTasks: Use clue cards to sort details that prove or do not prove the main idea.
Record a 20-second detective report explaining the strongest evidence.
Build a main-idea badge with one sentence and two proof stickers.
reward: Unlock the Evidence Detective badge after a new-passage transfer task.

sections.warmup: Look at four picture clues and guess what they all have in common.
sections.teach: The main idea is what a text is mostly about. Strong details prove the main idea instead of adding random facts.
sections.guidedPractice: Read a short paragraph and drag two details onto the evidence board.
sections.independentPractice: Choose the best main idea and explain why two details support it.
sections.activity: Create a detective board with one main idea and two evidence cards.
sections.reteach: Ask what all the details have in common before choosing a main idea.
sections.challenge: Find one detail that is interesting but does not support the main idea.

quiz.prompt: What is the main idea of a paragraph?
choices: What the text is mostly about
The first name in the text
quiz.explanation: The main idea tells what the whole paragraph is mostly about.

quiz.prompt: Which detail best supports a passage about how bees help plants?
choices: A flower can be drawn with crayons
quiz.explanation: Moving pollen explains how bees help plants.

studentFacing.mission: Become a text detective and prove the big idea with the strongest clues.
studentFacing.whyItMatters: Reading gets easier when you can separate the author's big point from extra facts.
studentFacing.bigIdea: The main idea is the one sentence that most of the details work together to prove.
modelSteps: Ask what most clues have in common.
Choose two details that prove the same big point.
studentFacing.example: If three details tell how bees move pollen and help flowers grow, the main idea is probably about bees helping plants.
studentFacing.nonExample: A fun fact about honey jars may be true, but it does not prove how bees help plants.
studentFacing.quickCheck: Can both proof details point back to the same center idea?
studentFacing.studentSummary: Main idea is the big point; details are the proof.
studentFacing.tutorHandoff: Tell the tutor if you are stuck choosing the big idea, finding proof, or rejecting a distractor.

learningObjective: Identify the main idea of a nonfiction passage and support it with two details.
successCriteria: I can describe the big idea in Main Idea Detective.
I can use a visual model or example to solve a new problem.
I can explain my reasoning and repair a misunderstanding.
I can retrieve and transfer the idea after a delay.
essentialQuestion: How can evidence help us identify the big idea?

knowledge: A main idea is the big point that the strongest details all help prove.
capability: Identify the main idea of a nonfiction passage and support it with two details.
Use a model, example, or explanation to demonstrate the idea.
reasoning: Use evidence from the model or task to justify a choice.
retention: Retrieve the core idea after the original lesson context is removed.
transfer: Apply the idea to a new example, context, or problem.

phaseModules.title: Notice the challenge
phaseModules.studentAction: Look at the model and describe what you notice about Main Idea Detective.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Become a text detective and prove the big idea with the strongest clues.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can say what I am trying to figure out before I choose an answer.

phaseModules.title: Build a model
phaseModules.studentAction: The main idea is what a text is mostly about. Strong details prove the main idea instead of adding random facts.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Main idea: Put the big point in the center only after checking several details.
phaseModules.successCheck: My model shows the important parts and how they connect.

phaseModules.title: Spot the parts
phaseModules.studentAction: Sort the examples, evidence, or steps that belong to Main Idea Detective.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Proof details: Details should connect back to the center idea, not just sound interesting. Distractor detail: A fun fact can be true and still not prove the main idea.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can explain why one choice fits and another choice does not.

phaseModules.title: Try the method
phaseModules.studentAction: Read a short paragraph and drag two details onto the evidence board.
phaseModules.visualSupport: If three details tell how bees move pollen and help flowers grow, the main idea is probably about bees helping plants.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can use the model to complete a new example.

phaseModules.title: Explain the why
phaseModules.studentAction: Can both proof details point back to the same center idea?
phaseModules.visualSupport: A fun fact about honey jars may be true, but it does not prove how bees help plants.
phaseModules.successCheck: My explanation names evidence or a rule, not only an answer.

phaseModules.title: Show your thinking
phaseModules.studentAction: Choose the best main idea and explain why two details support it.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Choose a drawing, spoken explanation, labeled model, or written response.
phaseModules.successCheck: Another learner could understand my reasoning from my proof.

phaseModules.title: Retrieve it later
phaseModules.studentAction: After a short delay, recall the key idea from Main Idea Detective without copying the original example.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Main idea is the big point; details are the proof.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can retrieve the idea when the order and example change.

phaseModules.title: Use it somewhere new
phaseModules.studentAction: Find one detail that is interesting but does not support the main idea.
phaseModules.visualSupport: A new context, example, or problem that keeps the same underlying idea.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can recognize when this idea is useful outside the original example.

phaseModules.title: Choose your next move
phaseModules.studentAction: Tell the tutor if you are stuck choosing the big idea, finding proof, or rejecting a distractor.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Pick a helper note, alternate model, reteach path, or challenge path based on your evidence.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can name what is still confusing and choose a productive next step.

feedbackRules.hint: Check whether every detail supports it before accepting it.
feedbackRules.action: Route to the alternate representation before retrying.

feedbackRules.result: Picking an interesting detail instead of the big point.

feedbackRules.action: Route to the alternate representation before retrying.

reteachPaths.trigger: The learner misses the model or cannot explain the key relationship.
reteachPaths.action: Ask what all the details have in common before choosing a main idea.

prerequisiteRepairPaths.trigger: The learner cannot identify the basic parts needed for the lesson.
prerequisiteRepairPaths.action: Use a short sort, match, or vocabulary check before returning to the main task.

challengePaths.trigger: The learner completes the proof independently.
challengePaths.action: Find one detail that is interesting but does not support the main idea.

parentTeacherNotes: Treat independent transfer and delayed recall as stronger evidence than one immediate quiz score.
accessibilityNotes: Provide text, visual, oral, and keyboard-accessible ways to demonstrate understanding.
Do not rely on color alone.
